name: Let it bounce, then drop
summary: Serve deep, let the return bounce before hitting it, and play a soft third-shot drop into the non-volley zone; count own faults and drops that land in the zone.
setup: Server at the baseline, partner as receiver; serve as your rules allow (the fault rules are UNVERIFIED in this app)
Receiver returns cooperatively, deep and soft, and stays back; the server lets the return bounce before hitting it (volleying the return counts as an own fault, `two_bounce`)
Server plays a soft third-shot drop aiming to land in the non-volley zone; the receiver catches the ball, so the rally is not played out
Rounds of 10 serves; swap roles after each round; count serve faults, two-bounce faults and drops that land in the zone
success_criterion: In each round of 10, at least 6 drops land in the non-volley zone with at most 1 own fault (serve or two-bounce)
coach_rationale: (judgment) On serve the serving side loses rallies with no opponent shot by faulting the serve or volleying the return; a cooperative serve-return-drop pattern trains both (AN-07 fault share) and the start of winning rallies on serve (AN-01) before live play. Unverified coaching content until a human coach reviews the library (P15).
